message.content: This codebase uses lowercase square-bracket annotations to enforce a strict machine-parseable metadata format. Lowercase ensures the comments are treated as identifiers rather than prose, making them safe to interpolate into strings, use as dictionary keys, or match against regex patterns without triggering case-sensitivity bugs. The square brackets provide unambiguous delimiters that parsers can reliably split on, avoiding collisions with code constructs like array access (`arr[0]`), string indexing (`s[0]`), or template literals. Together, they create a lightweight, zero-cost annotation system that remains invisible to humans reading the code while being perfectly readable by tooling that extracts type hints, dependencies, or behavioral contracts.
